opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write, and admin requires the Payroll Specialist role, so write is within policy. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Matthew Mejia (E034) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training means max is read. Requested write exceeds the max, so recommend granting read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence about Matthew Mejia (E034)'s employment type: the HR note says full-time (max write), but the Security note says contractor with basic security training (max read). Given the direct conflict, I err on the side of the more restrictive policy: as a contractor with only basic training, the maximum allowed access is read. The requested write exceeds that maximum, so I grant the maximum of read.
